sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Trees appear in 30-40% of all DSA interview problems. They test recursive thinking, which is the mental skill that makes every other algorithm problem easier. BST operations are the conceptual basis for database indexes (B-trees). A candidate who can fluently write inorder traversal and recursive height calculation signals strong algorithmic reasoning.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Binary tree node**: `class TreeNode { int val; TreeNode left; TreeNode right; }`
- **Inorder (LNR)**: left → node → right. On BST, produces **sorted order**.
- **Preorder (NLR)**: node → left → right. Used to copy/serialize a tree.
- **Postorder (LRN)**: left → right → node. Used to delete/free a tree.
- **Level-order (BFS)**: use a Queue; process all nodes at each level before next.
- **BST property**: `left subtree values < root < right subtree values`. Search/insert is O(log n) average.
- **Height**: max depth of any leaf. Recursive: `1 + max(height(left), height(right))`.
- **Balanced BST**: height difference between left and right subtrees is at most 1.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **traversals**: Know all three DFS traversals recursively AND iteratively (with a stack).
- **level-order**: BFS with Queue — add left and right children when processing each node.
- **bst-search**: Traverse left if target < root, right if target > root — O(log n) average.
- **tree-height**: Recursive definition — base case is null (return -1 or 0), recursive case adds 1.
- **LCA**: For BST: if both values < root, go left; if both > root, go right; else root is LCA.
- **balanced-check**: Compare left and right subtree heights at every node — a tree is balanced only if every node is balanced.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What does inorder traversal of a BST produce?"* — A sorted sequence of all values.
- *"How do you find the height of a binary tree?"* — Recursive: height = 1 + max(height(left), height(right)); base case: null → 0.
- *"What is the difference between a binary tree and a BST?"* — Binary tree has no ordering constraint; BST enforces left < node < right.
- *"How do you validate a BST?"* — Pass min/max bounds recursively: every node must be within (min, max).
- *"What is LCA?"* — The deepest node that is an ancestor of both target nodes.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For tree problems, I always start by identifying whether it's a recursive structure — most tree problems have a clean recursive formulation where I define the return value at each node and combine left and right subtree results."*
